Container.Name: MyMediaDB
Container.Overview: Self-hosted media catalog: scans your library folders, reads the technical metadata with ffprobe, matches titles against TMDB, TheTVDB and MusicBrainz, and keeps every field editable by you. SQLite plus an API, no external database server.
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: metadata tmdb scraper nfo tinymediamanager jellyfin kodi plex emby musicbrainz artwork catalog library
Container.Description:
MyMediaDB is a personal media catalog that runs on your own server. It scans your library folders, reads the technical metadata of each file with ffprobe, and pulls data from external sources only when you ask for it. Your database is the source of truth; NFO export is optional.
Think of it as a library manager in the spirit of tinyMediaManager, plus your own private TMDB for the cases where the public catalog gets the title, the artwork or the taxonomy wrong.
### There is no authentication yet
Anyone who reaches the port can read and **change** the catalog. Keep it on the LAN, or put it behind a reverse proxy with access control. Do not publish the port to the internet.
### First start
1. Open the WebUI. There is no login screen: go straight to adding a library. 2. Add a library and pick the folder **inside the container**, for example `/media/movies`. 3. Press **Scan**. Matching, enrichment and NFO export run at the end of the scan, so a new file is processed without a second click. Uncertain matches wait in the review queue.
### Provider keys
Every key is optional and the app also accepts them from the UI, where the UI value wins. Without keys the app runs and the external providers stay off; the scan still catalogs files locally. MusicBrainz and Cover Art Archive need no key.
### Container notes
- `/media` is mounted **read-write** on purpose: the NFO and artwork export writes next to your files. It never renames, moves or deletes them. - `/data` holds the SQLite database, downloaded artwork, the yt-dlp binary and the backups folder. Back it up as one folder. - ffmpeg/ffprobe, sqlite and Chromaprint (`fpcalc`) are inside the image. yt-dlp is downloaded on first use, so the container needs outbound internet for that feature. - The image runs as its own non-root user by default. The template adds `--user 99:100` so appdata stays `nobody:users` like every other Unraid container. - The image ships a healthcheck (`GET /api/v1/health`), so the Unraid icon turns green when the app is up. - Pre-1.0 software: the schema is versioned and migrations run on start, but read the release notes before a big upgrade.
### What it does and does not do
It catalogs and enriches: scan, match, review queue, override layer, NFO export, music vertical, and a `/api/v1` API with a TMDB-compatible namespace. It does not play media and it is not a Jellyfin/Plex replacement: it feeds them. A Jellyfin-compatible server from the same author is listed as the `Tinyfin` app.
Project documentation: https://github.com/rafaelvieiras/my-media-db

Config.Name: WebUI
Config.Description: HTTP port for the WebUI and the REST API.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: SQLite database, downloaded artwork and backups. Keep it on a path you back up.

Config.Name: Media
Config.Description: Your library. Mounted read-write because the NFO and artwork export writes next to the files. It never renames or moves them.

Config.Name: TMDB read token
Config.Description: TMDB v4 read token, the preferred one. Optional: without it the external providers stay off.

Config.Name: TMDB API key
Config.Description: TMDB v3 key, an alternative to the v4 token. One of the two is enough.

Config.Name: fanart.tv API key
Config.Description: Artwork only: extra posters, backgrounds and stills.

Config.Name: TheTVDB API key
Config.Description: Series enrichment. The variable is TTDB, not TVDB, on purpose.

Config.Name: AcoustID client key
Config.Description: Audio fingerprint lookup for music files. Needs Chromaprint, which the image bundles.
